source_tree_identity.method: content-addressable git tree-object comparison (git rev-parse <commit>:<path>) between e0775e6 -- the commit the manifest's authoritative deterministic_source_tree_sha256 (11802d0e...) was computed from -- and current HEAD, for every path in the hashed prediction source tree. This is a stronger, unambiguous proof than re-deriving the bespoke sha256-over-sorted-file-list algorithm from scratch, since git tree hashes are content-addressed: two matching tree hashes guarantee byte-identical contents for every file underneath, full stop.

source_tree_identity.reproduction_caveat: a fresh `git clone` + checkout of 829f586 followed by an independent re-implementation of the manifest's own 'sha256 over sorted (path, bytes) pairs' description produced a DIFFERENT hash (274d245c7b91ab511d6875d7b327c9fc0ddc2b98a0ca3a4de9a613f35b6f4830) than the recorded deterministic_source_tree_sha256 (11802d0e5afa769bb263435dff0329ed39092fa1de1b5efe1b4cbe078895f98c), despite an identical file count (159) and identical core.autocrlf=true setting in both the clone and this repo. This is attributed to not having the exact original hashing script (the manifest's prose description underspecifies path formatting / concatenation order), not to a content change -- the git tree-hash comparison above proves content identity independently of any bespoke hash implementation. Recorded here rather than silently reconciled or hidden.
